posts.cooked:
So, playing around in the video game with the F5 variants released so far:

This is the first version of Bunker where I use his base power almost every turn, even if I have Flak Cannon in the opening draw. It's also resulting in me actually using his non-Turret mode cards more often. A play phase, getting someone else a card play and then drawing two cards (and DR) because Recharge Mode was on top of Bunker's deck? Good stuff.

I had a friend play F5 Tachyon in the physical game, so I knew what I was getting into here. Not a bad power, sorta like an at-will Hyperspeed Barrage. If she has any damage boosts, though, it becomes insane. Being able to Hyperspeed Barrage and then do double or triple that damage on the same turn is nuts.

F5 Wraith synergizes really well with all the card draw she gets, though I have to be careful about not running out of cards, considering that it stacks. It's fantastic paired with Infrared Eyepiece and the Utility Belt, and everyone likes extra card draws. 

I've played F5 Absolute Zero before and he's by far my favorite version of him. Fishing for his ongoings doubles his set-up speed, and with his modules out it doubles as a damaging power. Being able to reliably put out Subzero Atmosphere on turn one no matter what can be a godsend and shrinking his deck makes it so much easier to find his equipment cards.

I haven't yet gotten a chance to play with F5 Legacy, but I can already see the possibilities. Extra card plays are always good, and being able to remove an environment card without actually destroying it is great for places like Rook City and Silver Gulch. The one downside of F5 Legacy is that without Galvanize, Tachyon's Blitz loses a chunk of potential damage.

Varients I really like:

Dark Conductor Argent Adept:  I think this power is really unique and versatile.  If you can combine this with some deck stacking, it's a really powerful tool to both get extra plays and to avoid some especially harmful Villain / Environment cards.

GI Bunker:  Situational, but I seem to often run up against lots of damage reduction and this power is invaluable for those.

XPW Captain Cosmic: I often find myself with base CC where I have 3-4 Constructs in play but don't have a way to deal damage (I never seem to get a Cosmic Weapon when I need it) and his base power is nice, but really hit or miss.  XPW gives me a little more consistency.

Best of Times Chrono Ranger: I have a love / hate thing going on with CR.  I think his deck is fun to play, for the most part, but can be underwhelming whenever I have to deal with a lot of damage reduction.  BOT gives me some more versatility where I can temporarily stack bounties on a new target on the fly.  Plus there's nothing more fun than chaining The Whole Gang!

Extremist Skyscraper: I love links!  So having both her Normal and Tiny cards play with those is a lot of fun for me!  I also really enjoy her Huge card giving consistent Enrivonment destruction comboed with damage that won't backfire on you when you have buffs.

PW and XPW Tempest:  PW is a great way to nova a Villain to death or, comboed with some Healing, just a good consistent extra play.  And although I haven't really been able to leverage XPW into being as useful as I think it can be, I'm still enamoured with its potential

Visionary Unleashed:  I'm not the biggest fan of Visionary's deck.  I never seem to have the thing I want when I want it.  But she has several solid Ongoings and Unleased lets me turn those into consistent damage.

 

Variants I dislike because they're significant downgrades

All Dark Watch:  I hate Dark Watch.  I really, really, really, really hate them.  Setback has been talked about here enough, but I agree with all of that.  Nightmist just plays too slow, plus if you have to use her power on consecutive turn, it just doesn't give you much.  I hate having to sacrifice Equipment or Ongoings to Fixer.  I think it's usually better to stack him up with some buffs and use his base power than to have him or another charcter be relegated to feeding his DW power.  And although Expy's DW power can be useful if you're not able to shoot someone, those times are relatively rare and even when they hit, you're probably better off getting an extra play over +1 next turn.

KNYFE Rogue Agent:  I suppose you could use some deck stacking to make sure you have bottom cards that you want, but it seems like doing damage will be the better option almost all of the time.

 

Variants I dislike because they're too good or otherwise don't fit my playstyle

Elemental Wrath Absolute Zero:  I'm a much bigger fan of base AZ than most people, so I don't see EW as a straight up upgrade.  Plus I typically use him to tank, and EW's inability to target himself is always frustrating to me

Team Leader Tachyon:  I don't particularly care for Tachyon's deck.  But TLT's power is so useful that I often find myself using her to just give everyone more draws while I build up for Lightspeed Barrage, which is pretty boring for most of the game.

Dark Visionary:  Same as TLT.  I don't like her deck, so most of the time I'm playing her, I just skip my play and use the power.

posts.name: Whovian
posts.cooked:
First-time poster here with quite a few thoughts.

Favorite variants:

  • F6 Tempest: He does get a lot of flak, and rightly so. However, I find myself with useless starting hands full of Shielding Winds often enough that the insurance of being able to draw a better round-2 hand (or just expanding options from an alright, but not great, starting hand) trumps the loss in earlygame damage. My philosophy is that, out of base and F6, you're only going to be using their base powers until a better one comes along, so pick the one which lets you graduate to a better power more quickly.
  • Every Legacy is fantastic.
  • Ra: Horus of Two Horizons: Same reason as F6 Tempest. He mines his deck for more options more effectively.
  • Setting Sun Ra: His power serves as a good panic button. In a recent game against the Chairman, he pulled a late-game Prison Break with all 5 Underbosses in the trash. The only way I managed to clear them out and win was with SS Ra's power and Grevious Hailstorm.
  • XPW Fanatic: Now many of her cards have a slightly different secondary use. Embolden self + Kill the Spirit + Sacrosanct Martyr + redirected damage from Embolden lets her aggressively torch down a target, for instance, especially when buffed. You can now redirect Divine Focus's high self-damage directly into the main villain's face.
  • F6 Wraith: This was my go-to Wraith before FV Wraith was in digital. In games where round-1 damage output is critical (e.g. Dawn, La Capitán, Chairman), the extra tiny bit of damage her base power lets you pump out can help greatly. She also gets something to do with one weapon and Utility Belt.
  • FV Wraith: Sets up more quickly and gives you something to do with cards you don't need.
  • FS Parse: Usually, when I play Parse, I want her to get her deck-manipulation cards out as soon as possible, and her power helps with that.
  • Termi-Nation Zero: I've gone back and forth on my thoughts on this variant. At this point, I've played enough Termi-Nation vs. Chokepoint matches where I drew nothing of interest for a while (even taking over half of Bunker's deck to draw a gun!) and AZ kicked in and torched Chokepoint to the ground at the last minute to currently love him.
  • PW AA: I often find base AA's power to be too weak to make much use of, and I'd usually rather spend the early game setting up as quickly as possible. PW sets up scarily quickly.
  • Adamant Medico: A boost in total HP recovery and a card draw seem worth the loss in focus.
  • F6 Bunker: He has some of the most reliable ongoing destruction in the game. Honorable mention to G.I. Bunker.
  • Cosmic Omnitron: Essentially a much-needed harder version of base Omnitron.

Least favorite:

  • XPW Tempest: Maybe I'm just not thinking in the right way, but I don't really see many situations his base power would be useful in.
  • PW CC: I really don't get him. His power seems too situational to be worth losing Fabrication.
  • FV Zero: I want to love him, and when he works he works wonderfully, but usually I find that when he finally gets a chance to set up, most of the work's been done already and he just deals the ceremonial final blow.
  • Dark Conductor/Kvothe AA: Given my praise of PW AA, this is a bit paradoxical, but his power just doesn't feel right.
  • DW Nightmist: While she isn't bad by any means, base Nightmist is my favorite hero and I find changing her flow so drastically a bit heretical.
  • PW Haka: I often find that he burns through his hand and doesn't have anything to do.
  • FV Bunker: While he is great, he doesn't really feel like a Bunker to me; his power seems aesthetically off.

F6 Tachyon, Dark Vis, and Hunted Naturalist deserve to be on both of these lists; I both love and hate them because they're too powerful.

Game-changing variants:

  • Rogue Agent K.N.Y.F.E.: Relies more heavily on her throwaways, but I often find the extra setup and support worth it.
  • Beacon: Rad
  • CC Requital: Sets up quickly, can be dangerous. My favorite combination.
  • XPW CC, Visionary Unleashed: Overhauls of ordinarily support characters with a focus on DPS of all things. I like them.
  • XPW Fanatic: Already discussed above; she's like other Fanatics in liking to lunge straight for the face, but a lot more intense.
  • DW Nightmist: To make use of her, your playstyle has to shift significantly to make up for her relative inability to feed herself needed cards. I find she bides her time more and is a less effective tank, and is much more aggressive, uncontrolled, and self-destructive when she lets loose. I don't like her for reasons stated above, but she is capable of beautiful things.
  • SS Tachyon: She becomes much faster and much less predictable; she's my favorite Tachyon for damage races because she builds up LSBs more quickly.
  • All the Termi-Nation Variants. Still have yet to really figure out Bunker.
  • Heroic Infinitor: A bit too easy, but fun nonetheless.
  • Skinwalker Gloomweaver: Now Gloomweaver is scary and no longer a punching bag who does nothing for the entire game. I still wish Challenge mode Gloomweaver did more to get his relics out.

Variants I'd like to see:

  • Variants for Tempest, Zero, Unity, and the Dark Watch heroes that aren't part of teams
  • Variants for Voss and Dawn.
  • Ennead variant? I feel there's a lot of potential there.
  • Vengeance/Villains team villain variants

I love PW Haka!  He has so much card draw that I rarely have this problem.  And the versatility of using Haka cards on other targets–not just heroes–is easy to miss.  Shield or Restore the Dreamer (especially in Challenge Mode), boost the damage of a hero with a damage rider (like Hypersonic Assault), or just make sure the team's tank has the highest HP despite an "oops" moment.  And don't forget you can play a Haka card and discard just one card to cycle through your deck faster and get to that Taiaha or Mere.

FV Bunker: While he is great, he doesn't really feel like a Bunker to me; his power seems aesthetically off.

I agree–it says something that the "best" Bunker is the least Bunker-like Bunker.  He's one of my least favorite heroes, and this variant makes him playable by just helping everyone else instead.  G.I is the only other version of Bunker I play, and only against the specific villains with massive damage reduction.
